scenes.say: Why does .NET handle memory so efficiently? What makes its garbage collection so effective?

scenes.label: CLR
scenes.sub: The Common Language Runtime manages code, memory, and garbage collection.
scenes.say: The Common Language Runtime, or CLR, manages your code, memory, and garbage collection automatically.
Garbage collection is split into generations. Gen zero for short-lived objects. Gen one for survivors. Gen two for long-lived data. And the Large Object Heap for really big stuff.
Most collections happen in Gen zero—fast and frequent. Gen two and the Large Object Heap are slower and less common, saving time by focusing on what matters.

scenes.title: dotnet-counters output
scenes.say: If you monitor a real app, you'll see Gen zero runs way more often than Gen two. The Large Object Heap can grow if not managed.

scenes.question: Are all objects collected equally?
scenes.wrong: Yes, every object is checked each time.
scenes.right: No. Generational GC skips long-lived objects most cycles.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Are all objects collected equally? Nope. Generational garbage collection skips most long-lived objects on each cycle.
